types.name: KnowledgeGraph
types.title: Knowledge graphs
types.body: Reusable bounded context shared by many roles, tasks, triggers and output recipes. The JSON body holds name and purpose plus a selection (rootTypes and selection: relationships, maxDepth, maxNodes), a saved GraphQL query (query, its sha256 hex hash, and variables as a JSON Schema), or both. With a selection, query is the GraphQL document the selection compiles to over the Wiki's generated schema, printed by graphql-js; without one, the query is the definition and reads run it as written. knowledge-graph.select runs the stored query when there is one and compiles the selection only when query is absent; a selection still bounds what a query returns. Legacy root_type and pattern properties remain an optional compatibility projection of a selection. Missing schema elements are reported as context gaps; this definition grants no authority or permission.

properties.name: root_type
properties.description: Starting node type registry name or UUID.

properties.name: pattern
properties.description: JSON relationships and max_depth. A relationship name defaults to outgoing; an object can select incoming. Optional: a saved GraphQL query without a selection has no pattern.

types.name: lens_for
types.title: lens for
types.body:
Attach a KnowledgeGraph node to a particular entity it explores. This describes a view, not a business dependency or access grant.

## For agents

Read from the knowledge graph definition to the anchor entity.

types.name: alternative_for
types.title: alternative for
types.body:
The source Product, Technology or Offering, usually a competitor's, is another way to achieve the target UseCase or UserStory, or something a customer could buy instead of the target Offering.

## For agents

Read this from the alternative to the scenario or offering it competes for. Record how it serves the scenario and how the target's organization differs, with a source. It records no partnership, endorsement, adoption or ranking. Use proposed status until the comparison is verified.

properties.name: status
properties.description: Evidence status: proposed, documented or observed.

properties.name: how
properties.description: One sentence: how the alternative serves this scenario.

properties.name: difference
properties.description: One sentence: what the target's organization does differently, or what the alternative lacks.

nodes.title: Offering dependencies and customer problems
nodes.summary: Understand what an offering packages, what those products depend on, who provides the technology, and whose problems it addresses.
nodes.body:
## Why this knowledge graph exists

Explore an offering through its products, dependencies, providers, source repositories, customer problems and affected segments. Follow only the selected recorded relationship types, up to four hops from the offering. Incoming experiences relationships connect problems back to their customer segments. Missing relationships remain gaps, not inferred facts.

nodes.title: Role operating context
nodes.summary: Orient an authorized person or agent in a scoped role: responsibilities, applicable governance controls, goals, measurement definitions and recorded evidence. Consumers supply the role assignment and scope; this selection grants no authority.

nodes.title: Organization overview
nodes.summary: Explore an organization’s projects and outcomes, products and offerings, customer problems, segments and recorded measurement context.

nodes.title: Competitive landscape
nodes.summary: Who else serves this organization's use cases, stories and offerings, how they serve them, how this organization differs, and which companies make or sell them.
